excerpt: In a musical landscape where virtually every new title promoted as 'jazz' would be unrecognizable to the musicians who actually created it, circa 1895, in New Orleans, it's refreshing to encounter a new release that not only acknowledges those pioneers but also respects and honours them.

album: John Lewis & Sacha Distel: Afternoon In Paris
excerpt: During the 1970s French singer and entertainer Sacha Distel performed a number of times at the London Palladium and on British TV. Long since deleted, it was a collectors' piece. Barney Wilen makes himself known from the off with a strong solo. John Lewis directs well from the front. An excellent reissue.

Pianist McCoy Tyner didn't let his path falter after the years with John Coltrane, continuing with powerful, high energy hard bop, his piano style full of blocked chords and melodic runs. From a live performance at the Umbria Jazz Festival in 1993.

Veteran French bassist Henri Texier is calling on past compositions of his to be applied as balm to brows fevered by the current anxiety-provoking atmosphere. Octogenarian Texier has been in the music business for six decades. The vitality of Healing Songs testifies to music as continuously inspirational.

There are times when clarinet-wielding Anat Cohen seems to have invaded and taken up residence in locations normally occupied by the saxophone. But she allows the clarinet to maintain and extend its character in her celebrated foursome Quartetinho by establishing a chamber-jazz format.

Jazz pianists overburdened with a classical technique can do the music a disservice. A bass player with one, who has performed in a symphony orchestra, may be better placed to experiment with mixing genres. On this often mesmerising album Mark Wade reimagines inspiring music from the concert platform.

This is the third album by the Nomad Trio. The evidence suggests a group that's thoroughly bedded in and at a point where mutual understanding ensures a unity of vision which hasn't coalesced into blithe.

This is a vinyl reissue of bass player Buster Williams' debut album as a leader, originally released on Muse in 1975, in which the concept is very much of the day, taking its lead from the 'electrified' atmosphere of Miles Davis's In A Silent Way and Bitches Brew.

Norwegian guitar supremo Hedvig Mollestad Thomassen follows her last album Bees In The Bonnet with the sophomore outing by her other trio outfit. Bitches Blues showcases her regular power trio at their best.

Some detect a Nordic influence in Lilly Hertzman's new album Heartshaped, but it is more reminiscent of Joni Mitchell's more jazz-influenced years. Poetic lyrics, strong melodies but with sophisticated changes, jazzy arrangements and some of the best international players you can find.

album: Gustaf Lunggren: Along The Low Road
excerpt: In a recent survey, Denmark and Sweden were deemed to be two of the happiest countries in the world and it is easy to imagine happy Swedes and Danes returning home after work and chilling to the music of Gustaf Ljunggren. This is gentle, relaxing music, carefully crafted and played with a deceptive ease.

The Italian duo B.I.T., made up of pianist Manuela Pasqui and saxophonist Danielle Di Majo, go to great pains to explain that their latest CD R-Esistenze is about resistance - the resistance movement during WWII and women's struggle for emancipation.

album: Elina Duni, Rob Luft: Reaching For The Moon
excerpt: Albanian-born singer Elina Duni is now on her sixth ECM recording, her third with British guitarist Rob Luft, this time just as a duo. She draws on a wide variety of languages and genres, covering traditional pieces, a Persian lullaby, an Italian ballad, Gabriel Faure's art song, all bookended by Irving Berlin's title song and Ornette Coleman's Lonely Woman.

album: Ahmad Jamal: At The Jazz Showcase, Live In Chicago
excerpt: In March 1976 Ahmad Jamal and his trio performed at the Jazz Showcase in Chicago. Everything Jamal plays here is beautifully delivered. Best of all is the concluding 21-minute Swahililand, a Jamal composition previewed in 1974 which manages to combine a whirl of profound pianisms alongside references to the English carol God Rest Ye Merry, Gentlemen.

Modha released their debut album Through The Cycle in 2023 and have now recorded their second offering. They remain in their tranquil soundscape, capturing the energy of live studio sessions and natural imperfections while retaining polished production. The Berlin-based jazz duo consists of Dhanya Langer and Max Scholl.
